environment.description: Same migration script deployed on EKS 1.29 with the following runtime configuration: (1) Pod runs with an ephemeral projected volume for DB credentials sourced from AWS Secrets Manager via the ASCP (AWS Secrets Store CSI Provider) with rotation reconciliation interval set to 30s and a custom rotation Lambda that invalidates the previous secret version immediately upon rotation (SecretRotationInterval=60s with ImmediatePreviousVersionInvalidation=true in the Lambda rotation step 'finishSecret'). (2) The pod's SecurityContext sets readOnlyRootFilesystem: true with only an emptyDir tmpfs mount at /tmp that has a 1Mi sizeLimit and is scoped to the pod's mount namespace (no hostPath). (3) A Kyverno ClusterPolicy 'restrict-signal-handler-creds' enforces that all pods in the migration namespace must have the annotation 'secrets.csi.k8s.io/rotation-poll-interval=30s' and validates the projected volume configuration. The net effect: even if an attacker reads the credentials file from /tmp during the signal handler race window, the credentials will have been rotated and the stolen version invalidated server-side within at most 60 seconds, and the tmpfs mount is not accessible from other pods.
